title: Noah, Brad DeLong, and Dan Wang discuss the Anthropic IPO
gist: Hexapodia relaunch episode on the Anthropic IPO: Noah Smith gives the bull case that frontier AI labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) will become oligopolistic conglomerates whose 'subsidiaries' in every industry tie up their capital structures to get access to proprietary internal frontier models, while Brad DeLong and Dan Wang are more skeptical. Smith cites a Google DeepMind model (Imas, Koh, Legg 2026) of AI breaking the Coasean ceiling on firm size, and discloses he will probably buy Anthropic stock at IPO.

themes.theme: Bull case: frontier labs as conglomerate parents

insights.claim: Noah Smith's Anthropic bull case does not require Anthropic to dominate all industries or AI to replace human workers; it rests on a change in the capital structure of the economy.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Frames Anthropic's IPO value around ecosystem/equity tie-ups rather than pure API revenue.
insights.quote: I’m envisioning a change in the capital structure of the efficiently producing economy.

insights.claim: Smith envisions that succeeding in any industry will require a tie-up with a frontier AI company offering access to an internal proprietary frontier model that stays months ahead of any model distilled from it.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: If true, the moat is the unreleased internal model lead; distillation-based competitors would remain structurally behind.
insights.quote: an internal proprietary frontier model that will be months ahead of any model distilled from it

insights.claim: Smith argues these tie-ups will not be arm's-length service purchases, as with oil, but will require companies to merge their capital structures with the AI firm so they effectively become its subsidiaries.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Watch for frontier labs taking equity stakes or JV structures with industry incumbents as the confirming signal.
insights.quote: every company in order to succeed must become a subsidiary of Anthropic, OpenAI, [or] Google

insights.claim: In Smith's scenario Anthropic would be the biggest fish in an oligopolistic ecosystem of a few AI conglomerates competing against each other via subsidiaries in every industry simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Implies winner-take-most economics concentrated in a handful of AI parents; long the leaders, short undifferentiated incumbents.
insights.locator: and Anthropic is simply the biggest

insights.claim: Brad DeLong and Dan Wang were both more skeptical than Smith about the Anthropic bull case.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Indicates the bull case is contested among informed economists; size conviction accordingly.
insights.quote: I give the bull case for Anthropic, while Dan and Brad are both more skeptical.

themes.theme: Theory: AI breaking the Coasean ceiling on firm size

insights.claim: A paper by Google DeepMind economists Imas, Koh, and Legg (2026) models that as AI coordination improves it can break the Coasean ceiling on firm size, triggering a phase transition toward large, concentrated AI-heavy firms.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Academic support for industry concentration driven by AI; relevant to antitrust risk and mega-cap dominance.
insights.quote: this can break the Coasean ceiling on firm size and the market structure undergoes a phase transition toward large, concentrated AI-heavy firms
insights.locator: Interestingly, some economists at Google Deepmind

insights.claim: The Imas, Koh, and Legg model finds that AI expertise is reproducible while human expertise is fixed in supply, and that increases in AI competence can initially change worker composition and decrease firm size before coordination gains drive concentration.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Suggests a two-stage path: smaller firms first, then concentration once AI coordination matures.
insights.quote: Increases in AI competence can change the composition of workers within firms and decrease firm size.

insights.claim: Smith's own version is more complex: humans and AI are complements, humans hold private data that AI is better at using, and one big conglomerate enters every industry while retaining human workers.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Proprietary data held by incumbents becomes the bargaining chip in tie-ups with AI labs.

insights.claim: Noah Smith discloses no current position in Anthropic but says that unless something major changes he will probably buy Anthropic stock when it IPOs, and he owns stock in TypeSafe, an Anthropic competitor.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Author has stated intent to go long Anthropic at IPO; note potential bias in his bull case.
